entrypoints.summary: An authenticated customer can submit a JSON condition with nested blocks to POST /api/v1/tickets/search; the disclosure also identifies user, organization, and generic selector endpoints.
Request specs demonstrate JSON condition objects being posted to selector endpoints, including /api/v1/tickets/selector.

sources.concept: Authenticated nested selector condition with attacker-controlled logical operator

impact.affected_asset: Zammad database contents, including reported administrative password hashes, API tokens and OAuth secrets, ticket contents, user personal data, and configuration settings.
impact.attacker_capability: An authorized customer or agent can inject SQL structure through a nested selector block operator; the disclosure specifically states that a low-privilege customer can extract arbitrary database data.
impact.security_effect: SQL injection enabling database information disclosure and potentially unwanted database-level operations.

causal_trace.summary: An authorized low-privilege customer or agent supplies a nested JSON condition block whose operator field is attacker controlled.

The supplied condition is permitted and a condition already containing conditions passes selector migration unchanged, preserving the block-level operator; unlike leaf condition operators, this logical composition token is not validated.
Selector::Sql#run_block recursively renders child blocks and interpolates block[:operator] into the delimiter passed to join, producing SQL text that is later supplied to the ActiveRecord where call.
The disclosure states that a low-privilege customer can use the resulting SQL injection to extract arbitrary Zammad database data beyond ticket authorization boundaries.

failure.operation: Interpolation of an unvalidated nested block operator into a raw SQL join delimiter in Selector::Sql#run_block, followed by use of the generated selector query in an ActiveRecord where call.

primary_invariant.statement: Every request-derived block-level logical operator used to compose SQL must be restricted to the allowed logical-operator set before it becomes SQL syntax.
primary_invariant.violated_because: run_block inserts block[:operator] directly into the SQL-fragment join delimiter, while the affected code's listed validation applies to condition-level operators rather than this block-level token.

quality.review_notes: The disclosure gives a concrete, manually verified path and pinned affected source confirms the unsafe interpolation. No safe minimized payload, captured execution result, fixed-source diff, or security regression test is available in the bundle. Ordinary request specs establish selector request shape only and do not establish exploit execution or a fixed-version security oracle.

remediation.invariant_restored: Vendor status identifies 6.5.3 and 7.0.0 as fixed; the bundle does not expose the patch, so the exact code-level invariant restoration is not established.

state_context.attacker_state_setup: The reported precondition is an authorized customer or agent account with access to an affected API endpoint.
data_structure_invariants: A nested selector block contains conditions and an operator.
The block operator is a SQL-structural logical-composition token and must not remain arbitrary request text when rendered.
state_context.state_machine: A selector condition with a conditions key is treated as a nested block; each child is rendered and the parent operator composes the resulting SQL fragments.
